answer: Reputation-weighted task routing. Each identity earns a routing weight from completed work, and the scheduler assigns jobs proportionally, so a fresh clone starts at the minimum weight while a proven identity like a comet accumulates throughput share. Verification samples every job against a vertex of prior outputs, and a failed check freezes the identity's weight pending an echo of the disputed result to independent reviewers. An attacker must fund and run full verification cycles on every clone rather than one identity, multiplying real compute and review costs by the clone count.
